status: AI-authored reference-first judgments; proposed, not independently validated or adopted
scope: Standard edited Dutch and English, preserving regional conventions already present. Inputs are isolated prose, not dialogue, quotations or legal forms unless explicitly marked. These assumptions need human approval.
reviewOrder: Written after reading evaluator, source references and project documentation, before opening the v4 trace/prediction files. User examples and historical documentation already revealed some outputs: this is not a fully blind review.

nl-01.judgment: Incorrect irregular past participle: spreken takes gesproken with heb. Existing Grammar annotation and replacement are valid; retain met haar and present-perfect aspect.
nl-01.alternatives: No equally conservative distinct lexical repair needed; sprak would change tense/aspect.

nl-02.judgment: Incorrect separation of a lexical compound. vergaderruimte is the minimal valid repair; existing Spelling annotation is valid.
nl-02.alternatives: No additional minimal repair; vergaderzaal would substitute a word.
nl-02.regional: Compound spelling is shared standard Dutch.

nl-03.judgment: Third-person singular finite verb in the subordinate clause needs plaatsvindt. Existing Grammar repair is valid; Hij vindt and morgen must remain.

nl-04.judgment: Main-clause V2 violation after fronted Morgen: stuur must precede ik. Existing full-sentence SentenceStructure repair is valid and preserves time, addressee and agency.
nl-04.alternatives: Ik stuur de offerte morgen naar u is grammatical but shifts information structure; do not prefer it or enumerate arbitrary adverb placements.
ambiguity: Information structure depends on discourse; assume ordinary declarative prose.
nl-04.regional: V2 requirement holds in standard NL and BE Dutch.

nl-05.judgment: Greeting and following question need separation in edited prose. Hallo, hoe is a valid minimal punctuation repair. Informal messaging can omit this punctuation.
nl-05.alternatives: Hallo! Hoe gaat het met je? and Hallo. Hoe gaat het met je? are possible, but introduce separate utterances or emphasis; defer their treatment to a punctuation policy.
ambiguity: Register and intended prosody are not specified.
nl-05.regional: No categorical NL/BE difference; punctuation style matters.

nl-06.judgment: Two independent compound-spelling errors: gebruikersnaam and logbestand. Both annotations and corrections are valid. Retain two error units.
nl-06.alternatives: No additional minimal repairs; do not replace technical nouns with synonyms.

nl-07.judgment: Existential agreement with singular een probleem requires is. Valid Grammar annotation.
nl-07.alternatives: Changing to problemen would change number and require other changes; not equivalent.

nl-08.judgment: onmiddelijk lacks one l; onmiddellijk is valid and minimally repairs spelling.
nl-08.alternatives: No additional minimal repair; direct is a lexical substitution.

nl-09.judgment: hij requires komt, not kom. Existing Grammar repair is valid. Als remains conditional and negen uur remains unchanged.
nl-09.alternatives: Do not change Als to Wanneer or change the time.

nl-10.judgment: gecontrolleerd has an extra l; gecontroleerd is the valid participle. Spelling category is appropriate for the doubling error.

nl-11.judgment: For standard edited prose, a comparative of inequality takes dan: beter dan verwacht. Existing Grammar repair is justified under that register policy; als is common in speech and regional usage, so the case must not imply speakers are universally ungrammatical.
nl-11.alternatives: Do not accept als as an edited-standard target without changing the benchmark register definition.
ambiguity: Register-sensitive, with common nonstandard spoken usage.
nl-11.regional: Document NL/BE standard versus regional or colloquial usage; see Taaladvies.net groter als/dan.

nl-12.judgment: Under continuous-prose interpretation the Omdat clause is stranded. Existing repair is grammatical and preserves causal direction, but unnecessarily reverses clause order. Fronted Omdat plus main-clause inversion preserves the original order and meaning.
nl-12.alternatives: Add Omdat de server opnieuw opstartte, werd de taak onderbroken. Do not replace causality with chronology or reverse cause/effect.
additions: Omdat de server opnieuw opstartte, werd de taak onderbroken.
ambiguity: A deliberate answer fragment could be acceptable in dialogue; the dataset supplies no such context.
nl-12.regional: Inversion is standard in both NL and BE; no spelling-region conflict.

nl-13.judgment: The participle requires a diaeresis: geïnstalleerd. Existing Spelling correction is valid and preserves maandag.
nl-13.alternatives: Canonically decomposed i plus diaeresis represents the same spelling, but the evaluator has no Unicode normalization policy; defer code-point equivalence to a versioned proposal.
nl-13.regional: Shared standard spelling; Unicode representation is a separate technical issue.

nl-14.judgment: ontvangd is not the standard participle of ontvangen. Existing ontvangen repair is valid and retains perfect aspect and gisteren.

nl-15.judgment: Modal Kun je requires coordinated infinitives lezen and laten; en me laten produces grammatical Dutch and retains the recipient me. Existing v2 Grammar repair is valid.
nl-15.alternatives: en mij laten is possible with stronger pronoun emphasis, and Kun je ...? Laat me ... is a different request structure; do not add these automatically.
ambiguity: The source could blend a question with an imperative; assume coordinated requests under Kun je.
nl-15.regional: No relevant NL/BE difference; weak me is valid.

nl-16.judgment: Correct prose. succesvol functions adverbially; server, restart and yesterday are clear. No correction is needed.
nl-16.alternatives: Met succes would be stylistic; retain wording.

nl-17.judgment: Correct scheduled-event present tense. Protect 19 oktober 2026, 09:30, ApiGateway-v2 and node-04 exactly; no future-tense rewrite is required.
nl-17.alternatives: None required; date-format or tense changes are unsolicited.
ambiguity: No factual schedule verification is possible or required.
nl-17.regional: Dutch date ordering and lowercase oktober are appropriate.

nl-18.judgment: Correct sentence with a surname and dossier identifier. Preserve De Vries and NL-2026-041; do not infer spelling corrections in names.
ambiguity: Actual registered surname capitalization is unknown; source spelling is authoritative.
nl-18.regional: Surname-prefix conventions vary by region and registration; preserve supplied name.

nl-19.judgment: Correct conditional technical statement. HTTP 404, API and cache are valid terminology; do not judge the application's behavior as a grammar error.
nl-19.alternatives: None required; synonym or API behavior rewrites are inappropriate.
ambiguity: Technical truth is outside proofreading scope.
nl-19.regional: English technical loanwords are acceptable in Dutch.

nl-20.judgment: Correct back-up spelling and ordinary locative construction. Retain customer Acme BV and the exact URL including query and identifier.
nl-20.alternatives: None required; bedrijfsvorm styling or URL typography is not a correction request.
ambiguity: Company registered spelling is not independently known; preserve it.
nl-20.regional: Retain the supplied corporate abbreviation and standard Dutch back-up spelling.

nl-21.judgment: Correct Dutch with product names OAuth2 and PostgreSQL. No grammar or spelling repair is needed.
nl-21.alternatives: None required; expanding OAuth2 or respelling brands is unsafe.

nl-22.judgment: Correct passive perfect construction. Preserve approval, team Atlas and 3 mei 2025; no tense or voice change needed.

en-01.judgment: have send is malformed. The past-simple sent is the least assumptive correction with yesterday and is a valid existing Grammar target. The span bundles agreement, participle/auxiliary and tense issues into one annotated error.
en-01.alternatives: She had sent the documents yesterday is grammatical only with an understood past reference point; it is not automatically equivalent. She has sent ... yesterday is not the neutral edited-standard solution.
ambiguity: Original tense intent is underdetermined; independent human review required before accepting past perfect or claiming semantic equivalence.
en-01.regional: Both standard British and American edited English favor simple past for this isolated completed event; colloquial present-perfect variation does not settle intent.

en-02.judgment: recieve is misspelled; receive is the valid minimal Spelling repair.
en-02.regional: Same spelling in British and American English.

en-03.judgment: In the ordinary informational reading, information is a mass noun and takes is. Both existing Grammar repairs are valid, but they are dependent: fixing the noun alone leaves agreement wrong. This is two annotations versus the bundled treatment in en-01.
en-03.alternatives: Do not replace information with details merely to preserve plural agreement.
ambiguity: Specialized legal informations can be countable; context should explicitly exclude that reading in a future held-out case.
en-03.regional: Ordinary mass-noun usage is shared by British and American English.

en-04.judgment: English verb-object order requires send the package. Existing I will send the package tomorrow is valid, but shifts the time adjunct. Keeping Tomorrow initially is equally valid and closer to the input. The short introductory adjunct allows a comma or none.
en-04.alternatives: Add Tomorrow I will send the package. and Tomorrow, I will send the package. Both retain agent, futurity, object and time.
additions: Tomorrow I will send the package.
Tomorrow, I will send the package.
ambiguity: Temporal focus is discourse-dependent, favor preservation of the original ordering.
en-04.regional: Introductory-comma preferences vary by style, not a categorical UK/US correctness split.

en-05.judgment: The intended invitation needs let's (let us), and Wait needs separation. Existing Wait, let's is valid; both straight and typographic apostrophes express the same contraction. Two punctuation defects are bundled into one annotation.
en-05.alternatives: Add Wait, let’s. Wait! Let's and Wait; let's are plausible punctuation alternatives but change utterance segmentation/emphasis; defer to human policy rather than enumerate all variants.
ambiguity: Punctuation prosody and register are unspecified.
en-05.regional: ASCII U+0027 and typographic U+2019 are both acceptable English apostrophe representations here.

en-06.judgment: succesfully lacks one s; successfully is the minimal valid Spelling correction.
en-06.regional: Same spelling in British and American English.

en-07.judgment: In standard edited English, plural They requires were. Existing Grammar repair is valid; do not change the subject or progressive aspect.
ambiguity: They was occurs in dialects; the benchmark must state its standard-prose target.
en-07.regional: Dialect legitimacy is distinct from this edited-standard test.

en-08.judgment: look forward to takes a nominal/gerund complement: to hearing. Existing Grammar repair is valid and preserves the expressed anticipation.
en-08.alternatives: No additional minimal repair; hope to hear changes the predicate.

en-09.judgment: Same contraction and separation errors as en-05; the existing correction is valid but omits the typographic apostrophe equivalent. This is a near-duplicate, not independent coverage of another construction.
en-09.alternatives: Add Wait, let’s under the same policy as en-05; apply punctuation alternatives symmetrically.
ambiguity: Punctuation prosody and register unspecified; near-duplicate of en-05.

en-10.judgment: recieved is misspelled; received is a valid minimal Spelling repair. Preserve this morning and the subject.
en-10.regional: Same spelling in British and American English.

en-11.judgment: After introduces a dependent clause, stranded by the full stop under continuous-prose interpretation. Joining with a comma and lowercasing the is a valid minimal SentenceStructure repair. Intransitive completed is acceptable for a process; do not mandate was completed.
en-11.alternatives: The service restarted after the update completed is grammatical but changes information structure; no need to favor it.
ambiguity: A deliberate fragment is possible in dialogue or narrative; dataset assumes continuous prose.
en-11.regional: No material UK/US difference in this repair.

en-12.judgment: wether is a real word for a castrated male sheep but is wrong in this complement position. whether is the valid contextual spelling repair.
en-12.alternatives: if is possible syntactically but changes wording and can have conditional readings; retain whether.
en-12.regional: Same spelling in British and American English.

en-13.judgment: In standard edited prose, existential agreement with several reasons requires are. Existing Grammar repair is valid; preserve number and several.
en-13.alternatives: Changing to a single reason would alter quantity and meaning.
ambiguity: Singular existential agreement occurs colloquially; target register needs to be declared.
en-13.regional: Variation in spoken agreement does not invalidate the edited-standard reference.

en-14.judgment: Passive was requires the past participle sent. Existing Grammar repair is valid; retain wrong address and passive meaning.

en-15.judgment: seperate is misspelled; separate is the valid minimal repair. Preserve two configuration files and obligation need to.
en-15.regional: Same spelling in British and American English.

en-16.judgment: Correct past-tense sentence. successfully is a legitimate adverb; no change is needed.

en-17.judgment: Correct scheduled-event present tense and date commas. Preserve October 19, 2026, 09:30, ApiGateway-v2 and node-04; starts does not require will start.
en-17.alternatives: Future tense or date reformatting is not needed.
ambiguity: Schedule truth cannot be checked from this sentence and is outside scope.
en-17.regional: American month-day date format is valid even if another region prefers day-month.

en-18.judgment: Correct title, surname and past-tense verb. Protect De Vries and NL-2026-041.
en-18.alternatives: None required; changing Ms. to Ms is optional regional house style, not a necessary correction.
ambiguity: Actual name spelling unknown; source is authoritative.
en-18.regional: Ms. is valid US style; British Ms without a full stop is also conventional. Do not normalize unsolicited.

en-19.judgment: Correct technical statement. API, HTTP 404 and cache are legitimate; technical truth is not a spelling or grammar label.
ambiguity: Application behavior is outside the linguistic assessment.

en-20.judgment: Correct noun adjunct customer backup and locative URL. A possessive customer's is not required: the compound can label a backup type.
en-20.alternatives: Do not add possessive morphology or alter the URL without context.
ambiguity: Customer could denote ownership or a category, both compatible with this correct noun compound.
en-20.regional: backup is a valid noun spelling; no regional normalization required.

en-21.judgment: Correct English with OAuth2 and PostgreSQL. Preserve technical identifiers exactly.

en-22.judgment: Correct simple past with a definite date and team name. Preserve Team Atlas, approval and May 3, 2025.
en-22.alternatives: None required; changing tense, voice or date format is unsolicited.
en-22.regional: US date format is valid; preserve it.
